v.why: Replacing a weak avg_pool with a 3x3 conv gives a much larger gain than replacing skip or other ops (experiments 48, 34).
Upgrading an avg_pool on edge 0 to a 3x3 conv gains about 6-10 points, versus 1.5-3.5 when replacing skip_connect.
Removing the direct 0->3 edge is catastrophic when edge 4 is also absent, since the output loses its main paths.
Replacing a conv on the final edge with avg_pool loses 3-7 points, more than replacing a skip.
Swapping the direct skip on edge 3 for avg_pool costs several points (experiments 8, 83).
Turning a skip on edge 2 into a 3x3 conv adds capacity and gains more than refining an existing conv or pool.
Replacing a strong 3x3 conv on edge 1 with avg_pool removes learned capacity (experiment 17).
Adding a skip on edge 3 helps most when edge 4 is absent and the output has few other paths (experiments 25, 24).
Replacing a pooling edge with a conv improves accuracy more than replacing skip or other ops.
A conv on edge 5 adds learnable capacity when edge 4 offers only a parameter-free skip (experiment 57).

raw:
These ten are my best-supported guesses, built from the 100 measurements and general NAS-Bench-201 behaviour. None were tested directly as a controlled comparison, and several rest on only a handful of cases.

- **Weak op replaced by a conv:** upgrading an edge from avg_pool or skip_connect to a conv should help more than upgrading from an op that is already strong. Experiments 31, 9 and 35 (edge 0 from avg_pool to 3x3, +6 to +10) compare with 67 and 2 (from skip_connect, +1.6 to +3.5). Similarly, experiment 48 (edge 3 from avg_pool to 3x3, +12 to +19) compares with 65 (from skip_connect, about -1).
- **Replacing a conv with avg_pool:** this should hurt more than replacing other ops. Experiments 64 and 18 (edge 5 from nor_conv_1x1, -3 to -7) and 17 (edge 1 from nor_conv_3x3, -2 to -7) are the evidence.
- **Removing edge 3:** this looks catastrophic when edge 4 is also none, since the output then loses its direct path. Experiment 43 (-74, -57, -27) is the main case, and it is a single data point.
